items.statement: Temporary equipment status information may be displayed on dry-erase boards or chalkboards instead of labels.

items.statement: Open, sample and reseal containers of materials in a manner designed to prevent contamination of their contents.
items.quote: the CGMP requirement that containers "be opened, sampled, and sealed in a manner designed to prevent contamination of their contents..."

items.statement: Sample containers or closures that purport to be sterile or depyrogenated only under conditions equivalent to their purported quality; a warehouse environment is not sufficient for this sampling.
items.quote: For containers or closures purporting to be sterile or depyrogenated, sampling should be under conditions equivalent to the purported quality of the material: a warehouse environment would not suffice
items.condition: containers or closures purporting to be sterile or depyrogenated

items.statement: As a minimum, perform any sampling of containers, closures and packaging materials so as to limit exposure to the environment during and after sample removal, i.e. by wiping outside surfaces, limiting the time the original package is open, and properly resealing the original package.
items.quote: At a minimum, any sampling should be performed in a manner to limit exposure to the environment during and after the time samples are removed (i.e., wiping outside surfaces, limiting time that the original package is open, and properly resealing the original package).

items.statement: Have well-written procedures for sampling containers, closures and packaging materials, and follow them.
items.quote: Well-written and followed procedures are the critical elements.

items.statement: A shipment of containers or closures may be released for use on the basis of the supplier's certificate of analysis and a visual identification of the containers or closures.
items.quote: Note that the CGMP regulations at 21 CFR 211.84 permit a manufacturer to release for use a shipment of containers or closures based on the supplier's certificate of analysis and a visual identification of the containers or closures.

items.statement: Once a supplier's reliability has been established by validating its test results, the visual examination of containers or closures may be performed entirely in the warehouse.
items.quote: Once a supplier's reliability has been established by validation of their test results, a manufacturer could perform the visual examination entirely in the warehouse.
items.condition: once supplier reliability is established by validating its test results

items.quote: Waste in excess of the normal operating rates may need (see 21 CFR 21.192) to be evaluated to determine cause (e.g., due to increase in sampling or higher than normal component defects...or both) and the consequences on product quality assessed.

items.statement: Demonstrate that processes are validated through process design and development studies as well as by demonstrating reproducibility at scale.
items.quote: The emphasis for demonstrating validated processes is placed on the manufacturer’s process design and development studies in addition to its demonstration of reproducibility at scale, a goal that has always been expected.

items.statement: Have a sound rationale for the number of conformance (validation) batches chosen to validate the manufacturing process.
items.quote: The manufacturer is expected to have a sound rationale for its choices in this regard.

items.statement: Use science-based approaches to process validation.
items.quote: The Agency encourages the use of science-based approaches to process validation.

items.statement: After identifying and establishing control of all critical sources of variability, prepare conformance batches to demonstrate that, under normal conditions and operating parameters, the process produces acceptable product.
items.quote: The CPG describes the concept that, after having identified and establishing control of all critical sources of variability, conformance batches are prepared to demonstrate that under normal conditions and operating parameters, the process results in the production of an acceptable product.
items.condition: after critical sources of variability are identified and controlled

items.statement: Successfully complete the initial conformance batches before commercial distribution begins, apart from the possible exceptions FDA describes in its process validation policy.
items.quote: Successful completion of the initial conformance batches would normally be expected before commercial distribution begins, but some possible exceptions are described in the CPG.

items.statement: Concurrent validation of an API may be used only when it is necessary to address a true short-supply situation and the concurrent validation study meets the conditions FDA sets in its process validation policy.
items.quote: the Agency would consider the use of concurrent validation when it is necessary to address a true short-supply situation, and if the concurrent validation study conforms to the conditions identified in the CPG
items.condition: true short supply and study meets FDA's conditions

items.statement: When concurrent validation is used to address a short-supply situation, perform expanded testing on each batch intended to address that situation.
items.quote: The conditions outlined in the CPG include expanded testing for each batch intended to address a short-supply situation.

items.statement: Confidence in the API manufacturing process may be gained by enhanced sampling (a larger sample size representative of the batch) and possibly testing of additional attributes.
items.quote: Additionally, confidence in the API manufacturing process may be gained by enhanced sampling (larger sample size representative of the batch) and perhaps the testing of additional attributes.

items.statement: Use validated analytical methods to test every batch, including validation batches.
items.quote: Validated analytical methods are needed for testing every batch, including validation batches.

items.statement: Under concurrent validation, use a validation protocol that includes a review and final report after multiple batches are completed, even if the earlier batches have already been distributed or used in the finished drug product.
items.quote: The Agency would also expect the manufacturer to use a validation protocol that includes a review and final report after multiple batches are completed, even though the earlier batches may have been distributed or used in the finished drug product.

items.statement: Base the justification for media fill frequency in relation to shifts on risk, depending on the type of operations and the media fill study design.
items.quote: A firm's justification for the frequency of media fills in relation to shifts should be risk based, depending on the type of operations and the media fill study design.

items.statement: For closed, highly automated systems run on multiple shifts with a rigorous media fill design, a lower total number of media fill runs may be justified, provided media fills are still performed on each aseptic processing line at least semiannually.
items.quote: For closed, highly automated systems run on multiple shifts, a firm with a rigorous media fill design may be justified to conduct a lower number of total media fill runs. Such a program can be appropriate provided that it still ensures performance of media fills for each aseptic processing line at least semiannually.
items.condition: closed, highly automated multi-shift systems with rigorous media fill design

items.statement: Incorporate activities and interventions representative of each shift, and of shift changeover, into the design of the semi-annual media fill qualification program.
items.quote: The 2004 guidance for industry on Sterile Drug Products Produced by Aseptic Processing states that "[A]ctivities and interventions representative of each shift, and shift changeover, should be incorporated into the design of the semi-annual qualification program."

items.statement: Normally repeat process simulation tests twice a year per shift and process.
items.quote: In addition, the EU Annex 1, Manufacture of Sterile Medicinal Products, states that "Normally, process simulation tests should be repeated twice a year per shift and process."

items.statement: For closed systems (not restricted access barrier systems) where the processing equipment design is robust and manual manipulation is minimized, this information may be taken into account when determining the media fill validation approach.
items.quote: For such closed systems,1 if the design of the processing equipment is robust and the extent of manual manipulation in the manufacturing process is minimized, a firm can consider this information in determining its media fill validation approach.
items.condition: closed systems with robust equipment design and minimal manual manipulation

items.statement: Evaluate a conventional aseptic processing line that operates on two shifts twice per year per shift, giving four media fills per year.
items.quote: For example, it is expected that a conventional aseptic processing line that operates on two shifts be evaluated twice per year per shift and culminate in four media fills.

items.statement: For aseptic filling in an isolator over two shifts, fewer than four media fill runs per year may be justified, while the line is still evaluated semiannually to ensure continued aseptic process control.
items.quote: However, for aseptic filling conducted in an isolator over two shifts, it may be justified to perform fewer than four media fill runs per year, while still evaluating the line semiannually to ensure a continued state of aseptic process control.

items.statement: Base any reduced total number of media fill runs on a sound risk rationale and reevaluate it if contamination issues occur (for example product nonsterility, media fill failure or any problematic environmental trends).
items.quote: This lower total number of media fill runs would be based on sound risk rationale and would be subject to reevaluation if contamination issues (e.g., product nonsterility, media fill failure, any problematic environmental trends) occur.
items.condition: reduced media fill program; reevaluate on contamination issues
